item.title: NLP Models
item.description:
A language model is a model that assigns probabilities to words and sentences. The probabilities should reflect word statistics in the training data. Probabilities can be very useful for many applications, e.g. for grammar correction, $$ \mathbb{P}(\text{This }\textit{means}\text{ in particular}) > \mathbb{P}(\text{This }\textit{mean}\text{ in particular}). $$

For model evaluation, extrinsic evaluation refers to performance measurements in real-world tasks like spelling correction or speech recognition. Intrinsic evaluation refers to calculating probabilities on some test set, to see which model outputs larger numbers. The common metric is the perplexity. For a test set $W=w_1\cdots w_N$, it computes $$ PP(w) = \sqrt[N]{\frac{1}{\mathbb{P}(w_1\cdots w_N)}}. $$
